headline: Seven majors below their 200-day lines, yet leveraged longs are paying to stay in the trade
paragraphs: Start with the map, not the candle. Every asset on this board, BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, BNB, DOGE, and ADA, sits below its 200-day average, and none carries a golden cross. BTC is 48.1% off its 12-month high of $124,739.81, ETH is down 60.2% from $4,817.76, and ADA is the extreme case at -82.4% from its own high. That is a uniform long-term downtrend across the board, not a split market. The 24-hour tape looks different: total market cap is up 1.56%, BTC is up 1.26%, and ADA is up 4.87%. A green day inside a down year is a bounce until the 200-day says otherwise, and today it says otherwise for all seven.

Momentum is where the picture gets interesting. RSI-14 readings are all mid-range, 41.6 to 61.0, nobody is overbought or oversold. But MACD splits the group: BTC, ETH, SOL, and XRP sit below their signal lines (bearish momentum inside a bearish trend, no argument there), while BNB, DOGE, and ADA have flipped above signal. That is a momentum divergence worth naming: a subset of majors is quietly accelerating off the lows while the trend structure hasn't changed underneath them. ADA's realized volatility of 74.5% over 30 days is the loudest reminder that this early momentum shift is happening on thin ice, not solid ground.

Positioning tells you who is funding today's bounce. Funding rates are positive across every asset with data (BTC 9.8% annualized, XRP 9.5%, DOGE 5.7%, ETH 3.1%, SOL 3.0%), meaning longs are paying shorts to hold their bets, and long/short account ratios are stacked long everywhere (XRP 3.04, DOGE 3.76, SOL 2.5). Liquidations in the past 24 hours ran heavily against shorts: BTC shorts lost $3.92 million versus $0.61 million for longs, ETH shorts lost $5.13 million versus $1.59 million for longs. That combination, positive funding plus short-side liquidations, reads like a crowd that bet against the bounce and got squeezed, not a market building fresh conviction from scratch.

Flows add friction to the story rather than confirming it. BTC spot ETFs posted a net inflow of $32.7 million on 30 Jul, but the five-session total is -$236.6 million with only 2 days running in the same direction, so one green print doesn't erase a red week. ETH ETFs were essentially flat on the day (-$0.9 million) and net -$83.4 million over five sessions. Stablecoin float has drifted down 1.6% over 30 days, a mild reduction in dry powder sitting on the sidelines. Whale wallets moved a net $112.7 million onto exchanges in the last 24 hours, led by a single $193.7 million BTC transfer to Kraken, even as $127 million in USDT moved off Bitfinex the other way. The weekly whale net has been genuinely choppy, +$903 million, -$96.8 million, -$126.1 million, +$953.1 million across the last four readings, which is oscillation, not a trend in either direction.

Sentiment sits at 25, Extreme Fear, near the bottom of its own 30-day range of 19 to 33. That's a crowd that says it's scared while the derivatives desk shows longs paying up and getting rewarded on a green day. When the gauge and the funding rate disagree this plainly, the disagreement is the story: spot sentiment hasn't caught up to what leverage is already doing. Worth watching from here: whether the 5-session ETF net for BTC or ETH turns positive (it hasn't yet), whether funding flips negative even as price holds up, and whether any major actually reclaims its 200-day line rather than just bouncing under it.
